name: DBHub
summary: Explore a dedicated database using SQL tools.
description: Explore a dedicated database using SQL tools. Available capabilities depend on the provider and the explicitly granted permissions.
about: Explore a dedicated database using SQL tools. Available capabilities depend on the provider and the explicitly granted permissions.
Windows initialize/tools-list and bundled in-memory demo SELECT returned fixture_value=7. Real DSN, database-enforced read-only credentials and authenticated databases remain unqualified.
SQL can read and modify database records; DSNs may contain credentials
Server code is free; remote database hosting may cost.

Read and write permissions are different. This recipe grants no automatic execution. Sara may still auto-allow tools from server read-only annotations; the owner must inspect and set host permissions before use.
Required: database-enforced read-only credentials. The SQL tool name or annotations do not enforce a read-only connection; writes must be denied by the database itself.

secrets.tip: Connection string for a dedicated test database using enforced read-only credentials. Stored in the vault; never use a production administrator DSN.

reaches: only the database host in your DSN
guide: Use Node 24 LTS; this pinned package requires Node >=22.5.0. Confirm node --version before setup; dependency presence does not check its version.
Provision database-enforced read-only credentials before adding this server.
Never connect a production administrator DSN. SQL tools are not automatically approved.
Only a bundled in-memory demo SELECT was executed, not a real database connection.
After discovery, open Settings → Coding → Tools and approvals. Set every tool in this server's group to Ask me first or Off before sending any request.
Save, leave and reopen the page; read back every tool setting. Repeat after restart, update or newly discovered tools. Stop if settings cannot be confirmed.

changes: First connection preview. Not published; qualification limitations are explicit.
